cultural.vision_reason: A Persian miniature painting with figures in a garden/architectural setting, elegant tilework and arabesque framing, and Persian calligraphic text panels, illustrating Jami's Haft Awrang (Yusuf and Zulaykha) — court manuscript painting made within the Persian tradition.

physical.title: Yusuf and Zulaykha (recto), from an Anthology of Persian Verses, including the Haft Awrang (Seven Thrones) of Jami: The Fifth Throne
physical.medium_raw: Gum tempera, ink, and gold on paper
physical.summary: The painting quotes verses from the Haft Awrang (Seven Thrones) by the Persian poet Jami, a classic of Persian literature, here illustrating the romance of Yusuf and Zulaykha. Originally rooted in the Qur’an (Surah Yusuf, chapter 12), the Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) encounters the wife of the Egyptian governor, traditionally identified as Zulaykha, both seated opposite each other on the right, framed by architecture.

location.made_in_place: Iran, Shiraz or Mashhad, Safavid period (1501–1722)
